overall: The AG found no violation for failing to create or post minutes, but found the Board violated the OML by failing to approve its backlog of draft minutes in a timely manner, and ordered approval plus training.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to document attendance, subjects acted upon, and votes for 2014 and 2015 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: although the Board created minutes from the relevant meetings

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to post minutes of 2014 and 2015 meetings to the Town website.
allegations.key_passage: The Law does not require that minutes be published to a website.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged minutes dating back to April 2013 were still being revised and unapproved, so the Board failed to approve minutes in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve minutes in a timely manner.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar conduct may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Approve the backlog of draft minutes for Board meetings held between 2013 and October 6, 2015 within thirty (30) days of receipt of the letter.
Review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law Training Video #5 (Meeting Minutes and Records) and certify compliance to the AG's office within thirty (30) days.
remedy_passage: review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law Training Video #5 (Meeting Minutes and Records) and certify to our office within thirty (30) days of this letter,
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
